text:
Anya: Infra-bot just posted a drift alert for prod vs staging. staging has a new NetworkPolicy denying egress to analytics, prod does not.
Devin: saw it, was that from the recent helm chart bump?
Anya: looks like the chart change landed into staging via the feature branch deploy workflow, but the gitops sync for prod skipped it due to an OPA policy gate.
Infra-bot: DRIFT DETECTED: path=clusters/staging/k8s/networkpolicy.yaml drift_type=manifest_diff severity=medium rule=restrict-egress-to-analytics
Maria: can you paste the plan diff from terraform? curious if there are Terraform-managed networkpolicies or if it's just helm.
Anya: grabbing plan now. here's the helm release diff and terraform snippet:
```
~ helm_release.redwood-app (staging)
  metadata:
    annotations: add network-restrict=true
+ networkPolicy.egress: deny to analytics namespace

~ terraform plan snippet:
  -/+ kubernetes_network_policy.app_restrict (new resource to be created in staging)
    ~ spec.ingress[0].from[0].namespaceSelector.matchLabels = { "env" = "staging" } -> null
```
Devin: so helm created the policy in staging, but prod's gitops pipeline blocked it via OPA? what rule tripped?
Sanjay: OPA blocked because of a global change to egress rules without a canary. policy: `require-canary-for-networkpolicy` flagged it. I can see the deny in the policy logs.
Maria: that explains it. But we also have a separate terraform-managed nodepool label drift: prod nodepool has label `gpu:true` while staging uses `gpu:spot`. That caused autoscaler config to treat prod as dedicated GPUs and we over-provisioned 3 extra GPUs last billing cycle.
Anya: impact note: estimated monthly extra cost ~ $4.6k for the over-provisioned GPUs. Ticketed finance already but ops needs to fix reconciliation flow.
Devin: proposed plan: 1) run gitops dry-run for prod with the helm release updated to include `canary: true` metadata for networkpolicy, 2) submit an OPA exception for the specific change with a short TTL, 3) run `terraform plan` for nodepool label sync and approve via infra-oncall if diff looks safe.
Infra-oncall: I can approve manual terraform apply during the maintenance window. prefer to do a canary rollback if anything flakes.
Sanjay: also recommend we add an allowlist for low-risk networkpolicy changes in the reconciler config (`reconciler.allowlist.networkpolicy_paths`) and create a runbook step that does a quick connectivity smoke test to analytics after apply.
Anya: creating a quick runbook snippet now -> will attach to the incident ticket. snippet: `kubectl run --rm -it smoke --image=alpine -- wget -qO- http://analytics.svc.cluster.local/health`
Devin: I'll open a gitops PR for prod with the canary flag and link the OPA exception. tagging @SRE for the maintenance window.
Maria: after reconciliation, let's add an automated check in CI that prevents helm/values changes to NetworkPolicy without a `canary: true` label and a matching smoke test. small CI job could run a dry-network-sim to validate egress selectors.
Infra-bot: REMINDER: runbook link created: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/networkpolicy-reconcile and ticket created INFRA-2247
Anya: nice. assigning steps: Devin -> gitops PR + OPA exception, Sanjay -> reconciler allowlist change PR, Infra-oncall -> manual terraform apply during window, Maria -> CI smoke test PR. I'll monitor post-apply errors in the console. :thumbsup:
Devin: PR up in 5m, will post link.
Infra-oncall: noted, will take the apply at 02:00 UTC.
Anya: closing loop here once prod shows the new networkpolicy and nodepool labels match staging. thanks all.
